A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NextHAM research and Materials-HAM-SOC benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hamiltonian prediction experiments, band-structure comparisons, runtime measurements, and component ablations on Materials-HAM-SOC.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds its own specialized-dataset predictions, a DeepH-E3 evaluation on Materials-HAM-SOC, and optical-conductivity comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix M introduces NextHAMcut-down: learned embeddings replace H(0) inputs, the output directly predicts H(T), and training omits the k-space loss. Figure 2 also revises the reported block order, placing TraceGrad after the feed-forward update rather than before it. The full framework retains its Hamiltonian correction approach, distance-based ensemble, and joint loss.

E1.justification: v3 adds material-specific prediction tasks on Monolayer Graphene and Monolayer MoS2, extending evaluation beyond the original cross-material benchmark. Section 4.3 also evaluates optical conductivity. Materials-HAM-SOC itself is retained: changing '68 elements' to 'more than 60' does not establish changed coverage, and the neon example already appears in v1's figures.

E2.justification: v1 compares against DFT, zeroth-step Hamiltonians, and internal ablations without external neural-baseline result tables. v3 adds an evaluated DeepH-E3 baseline on Materials-HAM-SOC in Table 5 and comparisons with DeepH-E3 and original TraceGrad on graphene and MoS2 in Table 7. The latter baseline scores are explicitly taken from Yin et al. (2025), rather than newly rerun.

E3.justification: The added specialized experiments use ordinary MAE, training without pretraining, and DeepH-E3's splits: 270/90/90 samples for graphene and 300/100/100 for MoS2. The main benchmark's split, Gauge MAE, and 100-epoch budget remain unchanged. Appendix I replaces v1's explicit feature-irrep specification with 392 channels in the first three blocks and a final-block representation expansion; this revises the reported configuration without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The six original component ablations, Table 4, and their appendix band plots are retained. Section 4.3 and Figure 4 extend the k-space-loss analysis to optical conductivity and report closely matched real-space errors for the compared models. Section 4.2 adds an OOD interpretation of the existing neon example, rather than a newly constructed held-out-element experiment.

E5.justification: Both implementation sections specify random seed 1 throughout training and inference. Neither version reports repeated-seed accuracy estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The runtime minimum/maximum/mean reporting practice is also unchanged.

E6.justification: The original accuracy, runtime, and ablation results remain unchanged, including the 1.417 meV overall Gauge MAE. New Table 5 reports DeepH-E3 at 12.605 meV versus NextHAM at 1.417. Table 7 adds graphene/MoS2 MAEs of 0.102/0.163 for NextHAMcut-down, versus 0.175/0.285 for TraceGrad and 0.251/0.406 for DeepH-E3. The optical case adds 0.53 versus 0.49 meV real-space errors and improved conductivity agreement with k-space supervision.

T1.justification: Appendices B and D add formal group and representation definitions and explicit mathematical treatment of TraceGrad's O(3)-invariant and equivariant constructions. These expand supporting formal material without introducing a new central theorem. The eigenvalue/eigenspace perturbation bounds and analytical gauge-parameter derivation from v1 are retained.

C1.justification: v3 adds an introductory claim of state-of-the-art performance in specialized DeepH scenarios. It also explicitly credits the established delta-learning paradigm while emphasizing H(0) as an informative input. The central contributions—NextHAM, joint real/reciprocal-space supervision, Materials-HAM-SOC, and accurate efficient prediction—remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 attributes the neon result to transfer through physically informed descriptors and acknowledges that broader element-level OOD evaluation remains future work. It interprets the conductivity comparison as evidence of improved wavefunction-dependent observables and expands explanations of embedding sparsity and DeepH-E3's generalization difficulties. The original ghost-state mechanism and large-system efficiency qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement supplies access links and extraction codes for code, pretrained models, and data. Appendix E specifies initial node/edge construction through inverse Wigner–Eckart conversion, tensor products, and distance-dependent decomposition. Appendix M documents baseline adaptation and the reduced model. One tradeoff is that Appendix I replaces v1's exact irrep multiplicity/parity list with a less specific channel-count description.

R1.justification: Beyond relocating related work to Appendix C, v3 substantially expands equivariant-model coverage, adds delta-learning and QH9 references, and develops detailed positioning against DeepH-E3 and TraceGrad. It also strengthens distinctions from molecular Hamiltonian methods around periodic-system subspace coupling and gauge ambiguity. These are substantive changes in attribution and research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 reorganizes the narrative by moving related work out of the main text, dividing the empirical section into statistical results and two case studies, and restructuring Appendix A.1–A.8 into appendices A–M. Extensive new background explanations, revised method prose, and reproducibility and other statements substantially change document organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds the four-panel band/conductivity Figure 4 and Tables 5–7, and revises Figures 1–2, including the architecture flow and explicit output converter. Existing result tables and appendix band plots are retained, with relocation and renumbering. The visual changes are targeted additions and revisions within the established presentation.

improvement.justification: v1 chiefly validates against DFT, H(0), and its own ablations. v3 addresses an important validation gap through external neural comparisons and specialized-dataset tests, while optical conductivity provides additional evidence for downstream physical accuracy. Initial-feature formulas and resource-access instructions also substantially improve reproducibility. The less explicit irrep specification and limited single-example OOD evidence temper these gains, but the added validation and documentation provide a clear substantial overall improvement.
